<ulSegoe UI”, Roboto, “Helvetica Neue”, “Fira Sans”, Ubuntu, Oxygen, “Oxygen Sans”, Cantarell, “Droid Sans”, “Apple Color Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Symbol”, “Lucida Grande”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 0px 0px 32px; padding: 0px 0px 0px 32px; vertical-align: baseline;“>
  • Prompt Payment: Encourages customers to pay outstanding invoices on time.
  • Minimum Overdue Balance: Set a minimum overdue balance to automatically generate the collection letter. If overdue is less than minimum overdue balance no collection letter is generated.
  • Fees & Blocking: Optionally apply fees to overdue balances and specify whether to block customer invoicing during letter posting/printing.
  • Customer Relations: Personalise collection letters using electronic reporting or Docentric to enhance customer relationships. The default report format is SSRS, but customisation options are available.
  • Open Transactions: Automatically lists all open transactions for the customer, reducing manual effort.
  • Multiple Collection Letter Levels: Create up to five collection letter levels in Dynamics 365.
  • Automation & Flexibility: Generate, print, and send collection letters with ease, apply interest to overdue balances, and build customised collection letter sequences.

  • How many collection letter stages do you need? (like 3 letter or 5 letters)
  • After how many days past the due date should each collection letter be sent? (this will be setup in days column)
  • What fee should be applied at each collection letter stage, and which main account should it post to? (remember only fixed fees can be applied)
  • What should be the payment term for the fees? (the terms of payment section determine the due date for fees charge when posting the collection letter)
  • Do you want to block the customer after processing the collection letter? if yes then at what collection letter stage do you want this setting?

  • 1st Collection Letter: Grace period is calculated from the invoice due date.
  • 2nd & Subsequent Letters: Grace period is based on the posting or printing date of the previous collection letter (as defined in Accounts Receivable Parameters).

    <h3Segoe UI”, Roboto, “Helvetica Neue”, “Fira Sans”, Ubuntu, Oxygen, “Oxygen Sans”, Cantarell, “Droid Sans”, “Apple Color Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Symbol”, “Lucida Grande”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 20px; line-height: 1.25; margin: 0px 0px 16px; outline: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9) none 0px; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline;“>Overview of Collection Letter Codes<pSegoe UI”, Roboto, “Helvetica Neue”, “Fira Sans”, Ubuntu, Oxygen, “Oxygen Sans”, Cantarell, “Droid Sans”, “Apple Color Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Symbol”, “Lucida Grande”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 0px 0px 32px; padding: 0px; pointer-events: all; vertical-align: baseline;“>In D365, you can generate up to five collection letter codes for a single transaction or customer.     <divSegoe UI”, Roboto, “Helvetica Neue”, “Fira Sans”, Ubuntu, Oxygen, “Oxygen Sans”, Cantarell, “Droid Sans”, “Apple Color Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Symbol”, “Lucida Grande”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 0px auto; max-width: 432px; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline;“><pSegoe UI”, Roboto, “Helvetica Neue”, “Fira Sans”, Ubuntu, Oxygen, “Oxygen Sans”, Cantarell, “Droid Sans”, “Apple Color Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Symbol”, “Lucida Grande”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 0px 0px 32px; padding: 0px; pointer-events: all; vertical-align: baseline;“>For now, let’s focus on how these codes are generated and what factors influence their creation.

    <h3Segoe UI”, Roboto, “Helvetica Neue”, “Fira Sans”, Ubuntu, Oxygen, “Oxygen Sans”, Cantarell, “Droid Sans”, “Apple Color Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Symbol”, “Lucida Grande”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 20px; line-height: 1.25; margin: 0px 0px 16px; outline: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9) none 0px; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline;“>Collection Letter Generation: Per Transaction vs. Per Customer<pSegoe UI”, Roboto, “Helvetica Neue”, “Fira Sans”, Ubuntu, Oxygen, “Oxygen Sans”, Cantarell, “Droid Sans”, “Apple Color Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Symbol”, “Lucida Grande”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 0px 0px 32px; padding: 0px; pointer-events: all; vertical-align: baseline;“>When setting up collection letters, you have the option to generate them either per transaction or per customer. The choice you make here will determine how the system assigns collection letter codes.

    <pSegoe UI”, Roboto, “Helvetica Neue”, “Fira Sans”, Ubuntu, Oxygen, “Oxygen Sans”, Cantarell, “Droid Sans”, “Apple Color Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Symbol”, “Lucida Grande”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 0px 0px 32px; padding: 0px; pointer-events: all; vertical-align: baseline;”>

    <ulSegoe UI”, Roboto, “Helvetica Neue”, “Fira Sans”, Ubuntu, Oxygen, “Oxygen Sans”, Cantarell, “Droid Sans”, “Apple Color Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Symbol”, “Lucida Grande”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 0px 0px 32px; padding: 0px 0px 0px 32px; vertical-align: baseline;“>
  • Per Transaction: Each transaction is treated independently, and collection letters are generated based on the individual past due transaction (Invoice).
  • Per Customer: Collection letters are generated at the customer level, taking into account all open and past due transactions (Invoices) for that customer.
  • This approach (Per Customer) raises an important question:

    <pSegoe UI”, Roboto, “Helvetica Neue”, “Fira Sans”, Ubuntu, Oxygen, “Oxygen Sans”, Cantarell, “Droid Sans”, “Apple Color Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Symbol”, “Lucida Grande”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 0px 0px 32px; padding: 0px; pointer-events: all; vertical-align: baseline;”>

    <olSegoe UI”, Roboto, “Helvetica Neue”, “Fira Sans”, Ubuntu, Oxygen, “Oxygen Sans”, Cantarell, “Droid Sans”, “Apple Color Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Symbol”, “Lucida Grande”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 0px 0px 32px; padding: 0px 0px 0px 32px; vertical-align: baseline;“>
  • If the next code is 3: This means the system is considering the highest code from all open transactions.
  • If the next code is 2: This means the system is considering the highest code from the oldest invoice (based on due date).
    • <pSegoe UI”, Roboto, “Helvetica Neue”, “Fira Sans”, Ubuntu, Oxygen, “Oxygen Sans”, Cantarell, “Droid Sans”, “Apple Color Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Symbol”, “Lucida Grande”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 0px 0px 32px; padding: 0px; pointer-events: all; vertical-align: baseline;“>As we can see that collection letter code generated is Collection letter 3 (In Identification section)

    <divSegoe UI”, Roboto, “Helvetica Neue”, “Fira Sans”, Ubuntu, Oxygen, “Oxygen Sans”, Cantarell, “Droid Sans”, “Apple Color Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Symbol”, “Lucida Grande”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 0px -24px; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline;”><pSegoe UI”, Roboto, “Helvetica Neue”, “Fira Sans”, Ubuntu, Oxygen, “Oxygen Sans”, Cantarell, “Droid Sans”, “Apple Color Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Emoji”, “Segoe UI Symbol”, “Lucida Grande”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 0px 0px 32px; padding: 0px; pointer-events: all; vertical-align: baseline;“>Hence the collection letter code for next letter will be the highest code among all the past due transactions included in that letter.
